drugInteractions.description: Combining Warfarin with Aspirin markedly increases the risk of serious internal and gastrointestinal bleeding.
drugInteractions.mechanism: Dual pathway hemostasis blockade (clotting factors + platelets)
drugInteractions.biochemicalPathway: Dual pathway hemostasis blockade (clotting factors + platelets)
drugInteractions.whyReactionHappens: Warfarin reduces clotting factors made by the liver, while Aspirin stops platelets from sticking together. With both safety nets switched off, bleeding risk multiplies.
drugInteractions.clinicalRecommendation: Re-evaluate whether both are required. If combined therapy is essential, monitor INR/bleeding closely and add gastric protection (e.g. pantoprazole).
drugInteractions.saferAlternative: Discuss with the cardiologist whether anticoagulation alone is sufficient.

clinicalRecommendations: Critical - Warfarin + Aspirin: Re-evaluate whether both are required. If combined therapy is essential, monitor INR/bleeding closely and add gastric protection (e.g. pantoprazole).
Warfarin: keep vitamin K intake (green leafy vegetables) consistent and check INR regularly.
Aspirin: take with food; report black stools or unusual bruising.
Lisinopril: monitor blood pressure, serum potassium and kidney function.
Metformin: take with meals; check kidney function and vitamin B12 periodically.
Older patient (72 yrs) on 4 medicines: review the regimen regularly (Beers criteria) and monitor for falls, dizziness and kidney function.
